descriptor: Precision engine parts plus aerospace and semiconductor machining
lede: A Bengaluru maker of crankshafts and connecting rods for two-wheelers and cars that is turning into an aerospace and semiconductor-equipment machinist. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32% to a record ₹1,091 Cr at a 19.4% EBITDA margin and ADS sales tripled (+207%), taking non-auto to 21% of sales. Returns on capital are still middling, about ₹800 Cr of capex is planned for FY27, and the stock trades near 67x consolidated earnings.

short_version.text: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue +32% to ₹1,091 Cr, EBITDA +48% to ₹211 Cr (19.4% margin) and profit after tax +52% to ₹109 Cr. ADS revenue was ₹164 Cr (+207%) and its backlog is ₹5,870 Cr over five years; peak annual revenue from other new orders rose to ₹2,241 Cr from ₹1,690 Cr in March.

ROCE is 14.5% after six years of 13-16%, capex of about ₹800 Cr is planned for FY27 (₹326 Cr spent in H1), finance costs doubled to ₹146 Cr in the quarter, and the Q2 deck has no Q&A, so August's high-teens growth and 19% margin guide is not yet updated.
About 67x consolidated earnings on Screener's 6 Nov data (the October version of this note used 76x standalone), at ₹4,414 per share.

blocks.text: Sansera forges and machines critical engine and chassis parts: crankshafts, connecting rods, rocker arms and gear-shift forks for two-wheelers, cars, trucks and off-road vehicles, in India and Sweden. Its ADS division machines complex parts for aircraft (Boeing and Airbus programmes, an engine blisk), semiconductor-capital-equipment makers and defence. Figures in this note are consolidated, as Screener now shows them (the October version used standalone, about 13% lower on revenue).

Often single or majority source for crankshafts and connecting rods; OEMs are outsourcing crankshaft lines to it.
ADS asset turns ~2-2.25x, auto ~1.25-1.3x.
Listed in 2021; consolidated revenue from ₹1,989 Cr (FY22) to ₹3,498 Cr (FY26).
Raised ₹1,200 Cr in a QIP in October 2024; borrowings fell to ₹407 Cr and debt/equity to 0.15x at March 2025 (0.24x at September 2026 after new capex).
Non-auto plus tech-agnostic/xEV now ~32% of sales, from ~12% at IPO; JV with Nichidai (Japan) for precision forging.

blocks.text: Sansera is executing well on a credible pivot into aerospace and semiconductor machining, with backlog to show for it. But the stock is priced as a high-growth, high-return business while its overall ROCE remains mid-teens; the payoff depends on ADS reaching its FY31 ambitions and lifting returns, not just revenue.
